subject: Post-call: Skybridge deployment constraints, target SLOs & topology options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.f@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.b@skybridge.ai>, ops@skybridge.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-06-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap and proposed next steps (SLOs & topology options)

Evan / Skybridge team — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap while items are fresh and to confirm alignment before we do a deeper technical dive. TL;DR: you have a high-throughput recommendation engine use case with tight p95 latency targets for interactive flows; we outlined three topology options (hosted multi-tenant, dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling, or VPC private deployment).

Pain points you emphasized:
- P1: p95 latency target for real-time recommendations ~250–350ms end-to-end (including network) for single-shot ranking calls.
- P2: sustained peak of ~80–120 QPS for the ranking endpoint; spiky bursts up to 220 QPS during campaigns.
- P3: data privacy — certain customers require VPC + customer-managed keys and 30-day retention.
- P4: cost sensitivity — need to compare unit token cost between a hosted approach (fast onboarding) vs Dedicated/Private deployment (better predictability).

Goals we confirmed:
1) Validate an architecture that meets 350ms p95 at 100 QPS sustained with graceful degradation above that.
2) Provide a throughput-cost model and a recommended initial topology (PoC baseline + production sizing).
3) Prepare a scoped PoC (4-week) to validate latency/throughput with a representative sample of requests.

Technical notes / assumptions from today:
- Typical input size: ~120 tokens per request, average output ~40 tokens.
- Preferred model family: you leaned toward a 7B–13B open model variant (we discussed 4-bit quantization feasibility).
- KV cache applicable for shorter session similarity lookups but not for stateless ranking flow.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
- Karthik: run a baseline throughput simulation (+ cost delta for quantized variants) and recommend a topology (ETA: 3 business days).
- Vivek: draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and measurable PoC success criteria (ETA: 2 business days).
- Naomi: share initial topology sketch, call recording, and send the Redwood security questionnaire + draft PoC SOW.

Attachments: initial-topology-draft.pdf (sketch), skybridge_call_recording.mp4 (call recording). I also captured the action items in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

If anything above is incorrect or you want to reprioritize items, reply-all and I’ll update. Otherwise, we’ll schedule the deep technical tune-up next week — Karthik, Vivek, can you both confirm availability for a 60-min deep-dive on Wed (7/1) or Thu (7/2)?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.b@skybridge.ai>

Cc: ops@skybridge.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed next steps (SLOs & topology options)

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: we’re lining up a small pilot with an enterprise retail partner, so the 30-day PII retention and VPC peering are hard constraints for that pilot cohort.

Additional details you can use for sizing:
- Average concurrent sessions during peak: ~140 (maps to bursts noted).
- Typical request size distribution: 60% short (<80 tokens), 30% medium (80–200), 10% long (>200).
- We prefer to avoid model warm-up penalties during campaigns; cold-starts that add >80ms to p95 are a non-starter.

Question: can you provide a rough ballpark monthly spend estimate for a Dedicated GPU pool that achieves 100 QPS sustained vs hosted usage at our projected token volumes? We just need a directional delta to feed procurement.

I’ll share a sanitized sample data slice (PII redacted) to help Karthik run realistic throughput sims.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Product Engineering | Skybridge Analytics
evans@skybridge.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>

Date: 2026-07-01T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed next steps (SLOs & topology options)

Quick technical thread — I started mapping requirements to three candidate topologies and have a short list of follow-ups before I run sims:

Clarifying Qs (Evan):
- Confirmed context window needs? if you have long inputs we need to size memory/KV strategy differently. Evan indicated majority under 200 tokens but 10% >200.
- Expected rps distribution across endpoints (ranking vs rerank vs embeddings) — you mentioned ranking is primary.
- Can you confirm tolerance for quantized model variants (4-bit) vs fp16? We should weigh latency impact vs small accuracy delta.

Initial thoughts:
- Hosted (multi-tenant) is lowest friction; likely fine for initial PoC but risks unpredictable p95 during noisy neighbors unless we isolate routes.
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) with autoscale + burst headroom looks like the sweet spot for your peak/burst profile — gives predictable p95 and easier KV cache placement.
- Private (VPC) is necessary only for customers with strict KMS/HSM and retention needs — we should scope that as an add-on for the pilot cohort.

Planned sims and deliverables (ETA 72 hours):
1) Throughput sim across input distribution you gave (60/30/10) with 7B and 13B quantized variants.
2) p95 latency curves at 50/100/150 QPS with cold-start scenarios included.
3) Cost delta table (hosted vs Dedicated monthly-run) at projected token volumes.

I’ll schedule a 60-min deep dive on Wed 7/1 11:00 PT; Naomi / Evan / Vivek — please confirm or suggest alternate.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
